paragraphs: FUNDVIEW sells an ERP platform to local governments, covering finance, workforce, utilities, community development, and court and citizen services. The pitch is aimed at cities running several disconnected systems and entering the same figures by hand in each one.

Every module posts into the same real-time general ledger, which is what removes the second entry. The finance side covers budgets, purchasing, payables, reconciliation, assets, cash receipting and reporting. Workforce management joins payroll, human resources and employee time onto one record. Court receipts reach finance as they are taken rather than at month end.

The company says more than 180 Texas local governments run on the platform. It states that fund accounting, financial statements and audit documentation follow GASB and GAAP standards. Payroll reporting covers 941, TMRS, TWC, E-Verify, new hire and year-end wage filings.

quote.text: Most local governments don’t have a software problem. They have a re-entry problem
